claims.content: To allow Customer Service Reps to suspend or deactivate customer accounts, with deactivation requiring a supervisor's authorization code.

goal.raw_text: To allow Customer Service Reps to suspend or deactivate customer accounts, with deactivation requiring a supervisor's authorization code.

claims.content: Customer Service Representative
The Customer Service Representative has access to the Customer History page, which is used by Customer Service Reps and allows accounts to be suspended or deactivated.
The Customer Service Representative has the applicable permission: “Permission to deactivate a customer account” or “Permission to place a customer account in review status”.
For a suspension, the customer has requested placement in “Review” status or there is evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity.
For deactivation, a Customer Care manager/supervisor authorization code is required to approve a permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
A Customer Service Representative uses the Customer History page to suspend or deactivate a customer account.

trigger.raw_text: A Customer Service Representative uses the Customer History page to suspend or deactivate a customer account.

claims.content: The Customer Service Representative accesses the Customer History page.
The Customer Service Representative searches for the customer by customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The “Results:” section includes Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, and E-mail address.
The Customer Service Representative chooses to suspend the customer account by placing it in “Review” status or to “Deactivate an Account.”

When the account is placed in “Review” status, the status means “suspended”; the customer can log in and change account settings, but may not bid, and the system will not generate orders for auctions-in-progress that the customer may win.
For deactivation, a pop-up DIV layer appears asking for a supervisor’s authorization code.
A supervisor’s authorization code is entered to approve the permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
Deactivated accounts will be listed in RED.

If the Customer Service Representative places the auction customer in “Review” status at the customer’s request or upon evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity, this suspends the customer account.

When an account is placed in review status, review status means “suspended”; the customer can log in, change account settings (for example, payment method), but may not bid, and the system will not generate orders for any auctions-in-progress that the customer may win.
If the Customer Service Representative deactivates the account, a Customer Care manager is required to approve, via code, the permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
For deactivation, a pop-up DIV layer appears asking for a supervisor’s authorization code.

Only supervisors know the authorization codes; the codes are issued by Administrators and generated by the Auction Admin application, and supervisors do not need Administrator access to input the codes.
Deactivated accounts will be listed in RED.

Exception path 1: If the required supervisor's authorization code for 'Deactivate an Account' is not entered in the pop-up DIV layer, the deactivation is not approved. Exit: the deactivation path ends without completing 'Deactivate an Account'.

Exception path 2: If the Customer Service Representative does not have 'Permission to deactivate a customer account' or 'Permission to place a customer account in review status,' the corresponding account action cannot be performed. Exit: the use case ends without changing the account status.
The customer account is suspended by being placed in “Review” status or is deactivated.

When the account is placed in “Review” status, the customer can log in, change account settings (for example, payment method), but may not bid, and the system will not generate orders for any auctions-in-progress that the customer may win.
For deactivation, a Customer Care manager/supervisor approval via code has been provided for the permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
Deactivated accounts will be listed in RED.
